new.title: UniPoolerCutoverEscrow.exitAndSeed can be permanently bricked for ~1 wei + gas by poisoning the empty canonical sUSDS/phUSD pair (sync'd dust donation or dust pair.mint); the escrow seeds only via Router02 behind a strict-empty gate and has no recovery mode
new.decision: NEW (not suppressed). Re-raise relationship to an owner wont-fix is DISCLOSED.

relatedLedgerTriageReasonQuoted.L-24: Owner triage 2026-10-01: wont-fix. Owner: "This is a mild inconvenience at most." Basis: a third-party dust pre-seed only trips the cutover's fail-loud reserves==(0,0) precondition, so the impact is delay on a one-off cutover; the griefer gains nothing and the skew is cheaply and profitably arbitraged back. Safe-recovery guidance retained (footgun): if the pair is pre-seeded, arbitrage it to the target ratio, then seed via direct transfer + pair.mint with a reserve-ratio assertion. Never relax the precondition or router-addLiquidity with zero mins into a skewed pair. Does not cover Q-19 ycn20q19 (pair not bound to router factory), which is triaged separately.

rationale: Different contract and newly introduced code: UniPoolerCutoverEscrow.sol is newInScope at 0fd6bdf; L-24 is anchored on UniPoolerV2.constructor (unchanged). Fingerprints do not collide.

Same underlying primitive (permissionless dust pre-seed of the empty canonical sUSDS/phUSD pair), but a distinct defect locus and fix: the escrow seeds ONLY via Router02 behind a strict reserves==(0,0) gate and has no mint-path recovery branch (CODE-001 recommendation).

L-24's wont-fix rests on recoverability: its triageReason prescribes the safe recovery as 'arbitrage it to the target ratio, then seed via direct transfer + pair.mint with a reserve-ratio assertion'. The escrow -- the artefact story-052 built specifically for this cutover -- cannot execute that recovery; a dust donor bricks this escrow permanently (redeploy fails identically), forcing abort() and an un-reviewed replacement seeder. That is new information the owner did not weigh on 2026-10-01.
story-052 itself asks this be raised with the auditor (L58/L224/L319/L343: 'DoS only; abort returns funds').
Cross-project corroboration: phStaging run-39 L-01 (2-wei pair poisoning blocks story-103 core; recovery seed must be atomic).
new.severityGuidance: Funds safe (abort() fork-proven to restore the old pooler); availability-only on a one-off cutover. Expect Low, consistent with L-24's 'mild inconvenience' tier. PATTERN-001's potential-high is a mechanical first-depositor mapping and should not drive the label. The human may legitimately re-apply L-24's wont-fix rationale at triage -- this record exists so that decision is made knowingly, not by silent suppression.
new.notRegressionOf: Q-19 098396142d (fixed): Q-19 is the non-canonical-pair half; this is the dust-pre-seed half (L-24 lineage). Q-19's fix (UniPoolerV2 L220-221) is unchanged and intact.

new.decision: NEW (QA/Info). Related owner wont-fixes disclosed; their tolerance rationale likely transfers.

relatedLedgerTriageReasonQuoted.L-22: Owner triage 2026-10-01: intended by design. Owner: "That's the nature of tolerance. We're literally tolerating an attack of this size." The keeper-chosen tolerance t is the accepted MEV budget; per-zap extraction is bounded at ~0.44*t*Delta (ECON-001) on protocol-owned liquidity only, no user funds. Disposition does NOT cover sibling L-06 (342075dfba, BalancerPoolerV2.pool), which stays open, nor L-23 (shared-venue floor staleness), whose stale-floor mechanism could widen the effective tolerance beyond t.
relatedLedgerTriageReasonQuoted.L-06: Owner triage 2026-10-01: wont-fix. Owner: "We're retiring BalancerPooler so definitely close L-06." Two grounds: (1) BalancerPoolerV2 is being retired (story-050 delete-balancer-interfaces-post-winddown, currently in incomplete/ at 2bfa090, so the contract is still live until it lands); (2) in the interim the same tolerance rationale as L-22 ycn20l22 applies: keeper-chosen tolerance is the accepted MEV budget on protocol-owned liquidity. Does NOT cover L-23 floor staleness. If BalancerPoolerV2 is NOT retired, or is re-used by new code, this disposition should be revisited.

new.rationale: Not suppressed: different contract (new escrow) and a distinct observable (minAmountsOut only checked length==2 and >0, token order unvalidated; seed has no ratio/peg band). L-06's own triageReason says 'If BalancerPoolerV2 is NOT retired, or is re-used by new code, this disposition should be revisited' -- the escrow is new code that exits the same Balancer pool. Value-leak hypothesis was refuted on fork (sandwich net-negative, ECON-001), so severity should be QA/Info.

new.title: Tight off-chain exit floors + public-mempool --slow broadcast let anyone revert exitAndSeed for ~$0.03 per attempt (Balancer swap past tolerance -> Vault AmountOutBelowMin); story-052's claim that the operator gate prevents the mid-cutover front-run revert is inaccurate
new.decision: NEW (QA/Low security half) + spec-conformance half F-01-052 (see specConformance).
new.rationale: No ledger counterpart; griefing of a one-off atomic cutover via a ~$0.03 Balancer swap past the floor tolerance. Funds safe (atomic, abort/retry). Complements DEDUP-003 (same floors, opposite failure mode).

new.title: Post-cutover the third-party 37.1% Balancer remainder stays a live second venue at the same price: part of the Stage-4 peg lift is arbitraged into it ($8-$11 at current depth; V2 settles ~$0.9735 not $1)
new.rationale: Not a duplicate of Q-21: Q-21 is plan-§5 zap sizing against seeded depth; this is the 37.1% third-party Balancer remainder persisting as a second venue that absorbs part of the Stage-4 peg lift ($8-$11). Per the externally-derived-yield rule this is opportunity cost on POL, not a value leak -- Info only. Fingerprint anchored on the escrow (whole-balance seed design); UniPoolerV2 is unchanged.
